the plasma β-end and plasma insulin concentrations were significantly higher in overweight and obese compared with normal weight prepubertal subjects.

the plasma β-endorphine concentrations in overweight and obesity children are positively correlated with the percentage of fat mass and food intake.

the possibility of using the plasma β-end level as an additional indicator of body fat, appetite and energy and macromolecular balance in overweight and obese children.
the possible role of β-end in the regulation of appetite in overweight or obese children.
the possible relationship between plasma βend levels, body fat and nutritional status in overweight and obese children.

β-end and insulin are involved in the regulation of food intake in overweight or obese children.

the β-end levels in overweight or obese children may be a useful indicator of body fat, appetite, food intake and insulin resistance.

the β-end concentration in plasma is an important parameter of body fat in obese children.
plasma concentrations of β-end are positively correlated with body fat in obese prepubertals, which is in accordance with the results of the study by Haffner et al. (1).
the β-end and insulin concentration is a useful indicator of appetite in obese and overweight prepubertal patients.

plasma β-end levels are positively correlated with the percentage of fat and food intake in obese children and therefore can be used as a potential indicator of obesity.
the plasma β-end level may serve as an indicator of the degree of obesity in prepubertal overweight and obese children.
the plasma β-end level can be used as an indirect indicator of appetite in children whose food intake has been restricted.
